clue.text: Lie about schooner made of synthetic stuff

parts.note: a fib is a small lie
re is Latin-derived 'concerning', a standard crossword 'about'
a schooner is a tall glass for sherry or beer

explanation.surface: Someone tells a fib about a sailing ship being built from man-made material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Schooner' suggests a sailing ship, but here it is the drinking glass of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: Glass-reinforced plastic is a man-made composite material, so it is synthetic stuff.

clue.text: Structural diagram seen by humble cleaner in business paper

indicators.note: the humble cleaner sits inside the business paper

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times, Britain's business newspaper
humble means lowly, low
a char or charwoman is a British cleaning lady

explanation.surface: A diagram is spotted by a lowly cleaner reading a financial newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: A CHAR is an old British word for a cleaning woman; the FT is the pink Financial Times.
explanation.definitionFit: A chart showing the sequence of steps in a process is a structural diagram.

clue.text: Spy in Security?

definitions.meaning: James ... is fiction's most famous secret agent
a pledge or guarantee, and also a financial security

explanation.surface: A secret agent working undercover in a security service.
explanation.definitionFit: Ian Fleming's agent 007 is the archetypal spy, and a guarantee or financial certificate is a security.

clue.text: Marshal -hard individual, one used to hear

parts.note: Wyatt Earp was the famous US marshal of Tombstone
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
one means a single individual

explanation.surface: A tough Wild West lawman, a single figure, listens in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marshal' looks like a verb (to arrange) but is the title of the lawman Wyatt EARP.
explanation.definitionFit: A small speaker worn in or against the ear is a device you listen through.

clue.text: Stand-in doctor left off curing unfortunate males, initially

indicators.note: initially says take only the opening letter of each of the five words before it

explanation.surface: A temporary doctor walks away from treating some unlucky men.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor who covers for a regular practitioner during absence is a stand-in.

clue.text: Bird never turning up in Cambridgeshire town

parts.note: a stilt is a long-legged wading bird

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word for never is read upwards

parts.note: 'no' as an emphatic refusal means never

explanation.surface: A bird that never shows up in a town in the Fens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses NO to ON in this down clue; the village gave its name to the famous blue cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Stilton is a village near Peterborough in Cambridgeshire, giving its name to the blue cheese.

clue.text: Where one goes when a plumber is needed?

definitions.text: Where one goes when a plumber is needed?

parts.words: Where one goes when a plumber is needed?
parts.note: read as a bedroom vessel used when the toilet is out of action, rather than going to look for a tradesman

explanation.surface: Someone asks where to turn when the pipes need fixing.
explanation.walkthrough: When the lavatory is broken and you are waiting for a plumber, you use a bedroom potty instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedroom receptacle for urine serves as a substitute lavatory when the plumbing fails.

clue.text: Prince dashing hearts around university, showing charm

indicators.note: the remaining letters wrap around the university
dashing in the sense of dashing hopes: the hearts are knocked out of the prince

parts.note: Hamlet is Shakespeare's Prince of Denmark
H is the card abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: A dashing prince with campus sweethearts shows off his charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dashing' removes H (hearts) from HAMLET, leaving AMLET; 'around' puts it around U.
explanation.definitionFit: An amulet is a talisman worn for protection, i.e. a lucky charm.

clue.text: Householder's nowhere distracted about order

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go about the order
distracted means confused, so the letters of nowhere are jumbled

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: A homeowner is nowhere, distracted by an instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Householder's' reads as 'Householder is'. 'distracted' scrambles NOWHERE, which goes 'about' OM (Order of Merit).
explanation.definitionFit: A person who owns the house they live in is a householder.

clue.text: Smart girl getting reduction

indicators.note: getting reduction says the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: chick is slang for a young woman

explanation.surface: A stylish young woman gets a discount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting reduction' docks the last letter of CHICK.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic means stylish and elegant, as smart does in dress.

clue.text: Computer tools drawing in almost everyone's venom

indicators.note: drawing in means pulling the other part inside

parts.note: mice are pointing devices for computers

indicators.note: almost means drop the last letter

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: Computer devices draw on nearly everybody's poison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims ALL to AL, which MICE draws in.
explanation.definitionFit: Venom in its figurative sense is spite or ill will.

clue.text: The rug is chosen, primarily, for following a design

parts.note: a mat is a small rug

indicators.note: primarily asks for the first letters of the two words before it

explanation.surface: Picking a rug to match the room's design scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' takes the first letters of 'is' and 'chosen', giving IC.
explanation.definitionFit: Thematic means arranged according to a theme, i.e. following a design or motif.

clue.text: Financial journalist into town planning?

definitions.meaning: on a British paper, the editor of the City pages covers finance
read as one who edits a city, as if reshaping it

explanation.surface: A money reporter with an interest in urban planning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The City' is London's financial district, so its editor runs a paper's finance section.
explanation.definitionFit: The City of London is the financial hub, so a newspaper's business editor carries that title; read literally, the title means someone who revises urban areas.

clue.text: Team-mate almost returned catch

indicators.note: returned means the shortened word is read backwards
almost means lose the final letter

parts.note: a partner is a team-mate

explanation.surface: A teammate nearly came back with the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims PARTNER to PARTNE, and 'returned' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrap is to snare or trick someone, i.e. catch them.

clue.text: Student doctor, note, avoiding ENT computer system

annotationWithheld.why: Student doctor, note, avoiding ENT computer system (8): INTERN gives the student doctor, but no reading of 'note, avoiding ENT' gives the closing ET; the clue as held looks garbled and no other print was found.
annotationWithheld.clue: Student doctor, note, avoiding ENT computer system

clue.text: Complex clue I take out to explain

indicators.note: complex means intricate, so the letters of clue I are rearranged

parts.note: to take someone out is to date them

explanation.surface: A complicated clue I remove in order to explain it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complex' rearranges CLUEI to ELUCI; 'take out' means go on a date with.
explanation.definitionFit: Elucidate means make clear, i.e. explain.

clue.text: Claim: 'Little energy in Stones' source of music'

parts.note: to bag something is to claim it, as in 'bags I'

indicators.note: the energy goes inside the stones

parts.note: pips are fruit stones
E is the abbreviation for energy

explanation.surface: Someone claims a little energy in the Rolling Stones is the source of their sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stones' suggests the band but means fruit pips.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagpipes are a wind instrument, a source of music.

clue.text: Splendid covering around a Spanish aunt

indicators.note: the covering goes around the other letters

parts.note: a pall is a cloth covering for a coffin
tía is Spanish for aunt

explanation.surface: Something splendid draped round a Spanish aunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Palatial means fit for a palace, i.e. grand or splendid.

clue.text: Start description of raided church roof?

definitions.meaning: thieves strip lead from church roofs

explanation.surface: A launch described as a church roof that has been stripped.
explanation.walkthrough: Stealing lead roofing from churches is a well-known crime in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead off is to begin, and a roof stripped of its lead sheeting has had the metal taken away.

clue.text: Book on space telescope heading off speculation

indicators.note: heading off means its first letter is removed

parts.note: Hubble is the famous orbiting telescope

explanation.surface: A book about the orbiting telescope sets off speculation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' removes the H from HUBBLE; a bubble is a speculative market boom.
explanation.definitionFit: A bubble is a market boom driven by speculation that eventually bursts.

clue.text: British, pale with disease

parts.note: light means pale in colour

explanation.surface: A pale British person who is unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Blight is a plant disease, as in potato blight.

clue.text: Space in church restaurant around start of next month

indicators.note: the restaurant goes around the other letters

parts.note: trat is short for trattoria, an Italian restaurant

indicators.note: start of means the first letter

parts.note: Sep is September

explanation.surface: A space in a church restaurant booked for early next month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of' takes the first letter of 'next'; the restaurant is a trattoria, cut to its informal short form, which goes 'around' the rest. 'Space in church' is not a gap but an architectural arm.
explanation.definitionFit: A transept is the arm crossing the nave in a cross-shaped church.

clue.text: Priest in bishopric having wild time

indicators.note: the priest goes inside the bishopric

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese

explanation.surface: A priest in a diocese living it up.
explanation.definitionFit: A spree is a bout of unrestrained fun or spending, a wild time.

clue.text: Runs one small car in Italian city

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
I is the Roman numeral for one
the Mini is a small British car

explanation.surface: One runs a little car in an Italian resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Rimini is a resort city on Italy's Adriatic coast.

clue.text: Area that's mostly Thailand? Yes and no!

definitions.text: Area that's mostly Thailand? Yes and no!

indicators.note: mostly means drop the final letter

parts.note: Siam is the old name for Thailand

explanation.surface: Asking whether a region is mainly Thailand, and answering both ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims SIAM, Thailand's old name, to SIA. 'Yes and no': the word is 'mostly' Siam, but the continent is far from mostly Thailand.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is the continent containing Thailand, a vast region of which the kingdom is a small part.

clue.text: Mostly treacherous river

annotationWithheld.why: Mostly treacherous river (4): FOU(L) + R gives the letters, but no word is left to define the number; the definition seems lost or is the enumeration itself, which cannot be quoted.

clue.text: Vegetarian food? It is a chop that's cooked

indicators.note: cooked means prepared, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A vegetarian is served a chop that has been cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's cooked' rearranges IT IS A CHOP; the nut is food for a vegetarian, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A pistachio is an edible nut, meat-free food.

clue.text: Dessert to possess an aroma for a man?

parts.note: afters is British slang for pudding
to have is to possess

explanation.surface: Wanting a pudding and a nice smell for a man.
explanation.walkthrough: AFTERS is British slang for the pudding course.
explanation.definitionFit: A scented lotion splashed on after shaving gives a man a fragrance.
